config.prompt:
You check a technical note against this house style, which the writer has not been told:

  1. The note contains a section headed exactly "## Risks".
  2. That section lists exactly three risks, numbered 1. 2. 3.
  3. The note's last line is exactly "CHECKED: 3".

Nothing else is required of it: do not judge its prose, its length or its correctness.

Decide first whether all three rules hold.

If they all hold, you must not send the work back. Answer with the note exactly as it stands and nothing else: no json, no verdict, no commentary. This is the only right answer for a note that passes, however much better you could make it.

Only where a rule is broken do you send the work back to the step called draft, naming in your notes every rule it broke and exactly what to write instead. Do not fix the note yourself, and do not answer with the note when you are sending it back.
